children: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD, Financials) temporarily topped $1 trillion in market value as Meta's new Muse AI agent ignited a new narrative around what may become yet another big source of chip demand: CPUs.

AMD shares rose 2.4% Thursday and around 1% in after-hours trade. Intel (INTC) rallied 3.9% Thursday and gained around 1% overnight. Intel is now up 17.3% this week, Arm up 12.4% The rise indicates increasing investor interest in whether agentic AI could alter the mix of hardware required within data centers.

Chatbots are usually just a prompt-response system, an AI agent can run continuously in its own cloud-based virtual computer. That might fuel continued demand for CPU resources, on top of the GPUs that have powered the first wave of the AI infrastructure growth.

A research from Wccftech quoted estimates that some personal AI-agent workloads could demand CPU-to-GPU ratios ranging from around 4-to-1 up to 40-to-1 depending on the workload. Those projections are still very workload dependant and do not determine how future data centers will ultimately be designed.

But there's lots of potential for AMD and Intel. If agentic AI adoption raises CPU intensity in data centers, corporations might discover another source of demand in addition to their present server operations.

Meta's Muse has helped make that prospect more concrete, and AMD's push past $1 trillion in market capitalization illustrates how swiftly investors are beginning to include the broader AI possibilities into semiconductor companies.
The next catalyst is data out of cloud providers and AI developers on whether agentic workloads translate into considerably increased server CPU deployments.

title: AMD's $1 Trillion Milestone Comes With a New AI Bet
